title: Media: intervyu va jurnalistika
goal_uz: Dars oxirida jurnalist savollariga tayyorgarlik bilan javob berasiz, asosiy xabarda qolasiz, yangilik uslubida qisqa matn yozasiz va fakt bilan fikrni ajrata olasiz.

scenes.title: Media bilan ishlash
board: Intervyu · asosiy xabar · yangilik uslubi · fakt va fikr
scenes.say_native: Assalomu alaykum! Oldingi darsda jamoani yetaklash tilini o‘rgandik. Bugun yana bir muhim ko‘nikma: media bilan ishlash. Kompaniya vakili sifatida jurnalist savollariga javob berish, asosiy xabaringizdan chetga chiqmaslik, yangilik uslubini tushunish va fakt bilan fikrni ajratish. Dars oxirida siz intervyuda o‘zingizni ishonch bilan tutasiz, qisqa yangilik matnini yozasiz va o‘qiyotgan maqolada tarafkashlikni payqaysiz. Uyga vazifa — soxta intervyuni yozib olish.
scenes.say: Welcome back. Last time we looked at leading a team. Today is about the media. You will learn to answer a journalist with confidence, stay on message, understand how news is written, and tell facts from opinions. Together these make you a clearer speaker and a sharper reader.
scenes.say_uz: Qaytganingizdan xursandman. O‘tgan safar jamoani yetaklashni ko‘rdik. Bugun media haqida. Jurnalistga ishonch bilan javob berishni, asosiy xabarda qolishni, yangilik qanday yozilishini va faktni fikrdan ajratishni o‘rganasiz.

scenes.title: Intervyu texnikasi
board: Buy time: That’s a fair question.

examples.t: That is a fair question, and I will answer it directly.
examples.uz: Bu o‘rinli savol, unga to‘g‘ridan-to‘g‘ri javob beraman.

examples.t: Let me put that into context.
examples.uz: Buni kontekstga qo‘yib tushuntiray.

examples.t: I would need to check the figures before I give you a number.
examples.uz: Raqam aytishdan oldin ma’lumotlarni tekshirishim kerak.

scenes.say_native: Intervyuga tayyorgarlik uch narsadan iborat: uchta asosiy fikr, ikkita qiyin savol va aniq raqamlar. Javob berishdan oldin vaqt yutish uchun: „That is a fair question“ — bu o‘rinli savol. Murakkab savolda: „Let me put that into context“ — buni kontekstga qo‘yay. Agar bilmasangiz, taxmin qilmang: „I would need to check the figures before I give you a number“. „No comment“ ni ehtiyotkorlik bilan ishlating, chunki u yashirayotgandek eshitiladi. O‘zbekcha „bilmayman“ o‘rniga inglizchada „I don’t have that information to hand, but I can find out“ — hozir qo‘limda yo‘q, lekin aniqlayman — deyish ko‘proq ishonch beradi.
scenes.say: Prepare three key points, two hard questions and your exact figures. To buy a moment, say: that is a fair question. When a question is complicated, say: let me put that into context. If you do not know, do not guess. I would need to check the figures before I give you a number.
scenes.say_uz: Uchta asosiy fikr, ikkita qiyin savol va aniq raqamlarni tayyorlang. Vaqt yutish uchun ayting: bu o‘rinli savol. Savol murakkab bo‘lsa: buni kontekstga qo‘yay. Bilmasangiz taxmin qilmang: raqam aytishdan oldin ma’lumotlarni tekshirishim kerak.

scenes.title: Xato: tez va sovuq javoblar
board: ✓ I can’t discuss that yet, but I can tell you…
✓ Assume everything is on the record.

examples.t: I cannot discuss the details yet, but I can tell you what we are doing for customers.
examples.uz: Tafsilotlarni hozircha ayta olmayman, lekin mijozlar uchun nima qilayotganimizni ayta olaman.

examples.t: I will not speculate on that.
examples.uz: Bu haqda taxmin qilmayman.

scenes.say_native: Birinchi xato — „No comment“ deb javobni tugatish. U „aybdorman“ deganday eshitiladi. Buning o‘rniga sababni ayting va gapni davom ettiring: „I cannot discuss the details yet, but I can tell you what we are doing for customers.“ Ikkinchi xato — „off the record“ ga ishonish. Bu iborani ayting-u, jurnalist baribir ishlatishi mumkin: har bir gap yozilmoqda deb o‘ylang. Uchinchi xato — taxmin qilish: „I will not speculate“ — taxmin qilmayman, deb ayting. O‘zbekchada bir gapni boshqasiga bog‘lab ketaverish odat, intervyuda esa qisqa, tugallangan javoblar yaxshiroq.
scenes.say: The first mistake is the cold no comment, which sounds like guilt. Give a reason and keep talking: I cannot discuss the details yet, but I can tell you what we are doing for customers. The second mistake is trusting off the record. Assume everything you say can be printed. And never speculate: I will not speculate on that.
scenes.say_uz: Birinchi xato — sovuq no comment, u aybdorlikdek eshitiladi. Sababini ayting va davom eting. Ikkinchi xato — off the record ga ishonish: aytganingiz hammasi bosilishi mumkin deb o‘ylang. Taxmin qilmang.

scenes.title: Mashq: qiyin savolga javob
board: Journalist: Your app crashed for two hours yesterday. Why were customers not warned?
scenes.say_native: Jurnalist so‘raydi: „Kecha ilovangiz ikki soat ishlamadi. Nega mijozlar ogohlantirilmadi?“ Javobingizda uchta narsa bo‘lsin: o‘rinli savol deb tan olish, bitta fakt va bitta amaliy chora. Shoshilmang va aybni yashirmang. Javobni baland ovozda ayting.
scenes.say: A journalist asks: your app crashed for two hours yesterday. Why were customers not warned? Answer in three steps: acknowledge that it is a fair question, give one fact and describe one action you are taking.
scenes.say_uz: Jurnalist so‘raydi: kecha ilovangiz ikki soat ishlamadi, nega mijozlar ogohlantirilmadi? Uch bosqichda javob bering: savol o‘rinli ekanini tan oling, bitta fakt ayting va bitta amaliy chorani tasvirlang.

scenes.title: Javob: qiyin savol
board: We are adding an automatic alert.

examples.t: The outage lasted one hundred and eighteen minutes.
examples.uz: Uzilish yuz o‘n sakkiz daqiqa davom etdi.

scenes.say_native: Namunaviy javob: „That is a fair question, and customers deserved better. The outage lasted one hundred and eighteen minutes, and our alert system failed to send a warning. We have now added an automatic alert, and we will email everyone affected today.“ „Outage“ — xizmatning uzilishi. „Deserve“ — loyiq bo‘lmoq. Javob aybni tan oldi, aniq raqam keltirdi va tuzatishni ko‘rsatdi. Ayblovchi savolga himoyaga o‘tmasdan javob bergan odamga ko‘proq ishonamiz. Sizda ham fakt va chora bo‘lsa, to‘g‘ri bajargansiz.
scenes.say: A model answer. That is a fair question, and customers deserved better. The outage lasted one hundred and eighteen minutes, and our alert system failed to send a warning. We have now added an automatic alert, and we will email everyone affected today.
scenes.say_uz: Namunaviy javob. Bu o‘rinli savol, mijozlar yaxshiroq munosabatga loyiq edi. Uzilish yuz o‘n sakkiz daqiqa davom etdi va ogohlantirish tizimimiz xabar yubora olmadi. Endi avtomatik ogohlantirish qo‘shdik va bugun hamma zarar ko‘rganlarga xat yuboramiz.

scenes.title: Asosiy xabarda qolish

examples.t: I understand the concern, but what matters most is that every customer is safe.
examples.uz: Tashvishni tushunaman, lekin eng muhimi har bir mijoz xavfsizligi.

examples.t: The key point here is that prices are not rising this year.
examples.uz: Bu yerdagi asosiy gap shuki, bu yil narxlar oshmaydi.

examples.t: We are building a service people can rely on.
examples.uz: Biz odamlar ishona oladigan xizmat qurmoqdamiz.

scenes.say_native: „Staying on message“ — savol qanday bo‘lmasin, o‘z asosiy fikringizga qaytish. Buning uchun „bridge“, ya’ni ko‘prik iboralari bor: „I understand the concern, but what matters most is that every customer is safe.“ Yana: „The key point here is…“, „If I can add something important…“. Soundbite — qisqa, esda qoladigan gap, o‘n besh so‘zdan oshmasligi kerak: „We are building a service people can rely on.“ Jurnalist ko‘pincha aynan shu gapni sarlavhaga oladi. Bu o‘zbekcha „gap aylantirish“ emas: siz savolga javob berasiz, keyin ko‘prik orqali o‘z xabaringizni qo‘shasiz.
scenes.say: Staying on message means returning to your main point whatever the question. Use bridging phrases: I understand the concern, but what matters most is that every customer is safe. Or: the key point here is that prices are not rising this year. A soundbite is short and memorable, under fifteen words: we are building a service people can rely on.
scenes.say_uz: Asosiy xabarda qolish — savol qanday bo‘lmasin, asosiy fikrga qaytish. Ko‘prik iboralaridan foydalaning. Soundbite qisqa va esda qoladigan bo‘ladi, o‘n besh so‘zdan oshmaydi.

scenes.title: Xato: savolni chetlab o‘tish va uzun gap
board: ✗ That’s not the point. (savolni rad etish)
✓ I hear that. What matters most is…

examples.t: We are not hiding anything; we are publishing the full report on Monday.
examples.uz: Biz hech narsani yashirmayapmiz; to‘liq hisobotni dushanba kuni e’lon qilamiz.

examples.t: What I can say is that safety comes first.
examples.uz: Ayta oladigan gapim shuki, xavfsizlik birinchi o‘rinda.

scenes.say_native: Uchta xatoga e’tibor bering. Birinchisi — savolni rad etish: „That’s not the point“. Bu mensimaslikdek eshitiladi. Avval tan oling, keyin ko‘prik qiling. Ikkinchisi — juda uzun javob: to‘qson soniyalik gap tahrirlashda kesiladi va noto‘g‘ri kesilishi mumkin. Javobni yigirma-o‘ttiz soniyada tugating. Uchinchisi — jurnalistning salbiy so‘zlarini takrorlash: u „scandal“ desa, siz „we are not in a scandal“ demang, chunki sarlavhada „scandal“ qoladi. Buning o‘rniga ijobiy ayting: „What I can say is that safety comes first“. Shunday qilib, hech narsa yashirmagandek va xotirjam ko‘rinasiz.
scenes.say: Avoid three traps. Do not dismiss the question with that's not the point. Acknowledge first, then bridge. Do not give ninety-second answers, because editors cut them, sometimes badly. And do not repeat a journalist's negative words. Say what you can: what I can say is that safety comes first.
scenes.say_uz: Uchta tuzoqdan saqlaning. Savolni that’s not the point deb rad etmang: avval tan oling, keyin ko‘prik qiling. To‘qson soniyalik javob bermang, muharrirlar uni kesadi. Jurnalistning salbiy so‘zlarini takrorlamang, ayta oladigan gapni ayting.

scenes.title: Mashq: ko‘prik va soundbite
board: Q: Isn’t your new fee just a way to squeeze customers?
Message: transparent pricing, no hidden charges
scenes.say_native: Savol: „Yangi to‘lovingiz mijozlardan pul siqib olish usuli emasmi?“ Asosiy xabaringiz: shaffof narxlar, yashirin to‘lovlar yo‘q. Savolni qisqa tan oling, ko‘prik qiling va o‘n besh so‘zdan oshmaydigan soundbite ayting. Javobni baland ovozda ayting.
scenes.say: The question is: isn't your new fee just a way to squeeze customers? Your message is transparent pricing with no hidden charges. Acknowledge briefly, use a bridge, and finish with a soundbite of fifteen words or fewer.
scenes.say_uz: Savol: yangi to‘lovingiz mijozlardan pul siqib olish usuli emasmi? Xabaringiz: shaffof narx, yashirin to‘lovlar yo‘q. Qisqa tan oling, ko‘prik qiling va o‘n besh so‘zdan oshmaydigan soundbite bilan tugating.

scenes.title: Javob: ko‘prik namunasi

examples.t: One price, no surprises, from the first day.
examples.uz: Bitta narx, hech qanday kutilmagan to‘lovsiz, birinchi kundan.

scenes.say_native: Namunaviy javob: „I understand why people ask. What matters most is transparency: customers will see one price, with no hidden charges, from the first day. One price, no surprises.“ Birinchi gap tan olish, ikkinchisi ko‘prik, uchinchisi esa to‘rt so‘zdan iborat qisqa, esda qoladigan shior. Savol salbiy bo‘lsa ham, siz salbiy so‘zni takrorlamadingiz: „squeeze“ so‘zi javobda yo‘q. Bu yerda „from the first day“ — birinchi kundan, „hidden“ — yashirin. Sizning javobingizda tan olish, ko‘prik va qisqa shior bo‘lsa, topshiriq bajarilgan.
scenes.say: A model answer. I understand why people ask. What matters most is transparency. Customers will see one price, with no hidden charges, from the first day. One price, no surprises. Notice that the answer never repeats the journalist's negative word, squeeze.
scenes.say_uz: Namunaviy javob. Nega odamlar so‘rashini tushunaman. Eng muhimi shaffoflik: mijozlar birinchi kundan yashirin to‘lovsiz bitta narxni ko‘radi. Bitta narx, hech qanday kutilmagan to‘lov yo‘q. Javob jurnalistning salbiy so‘zini takrorlamaydi.

scenes.title: Yangilik yozish uslubi

examples.t: City bus fares to rise by 5 per cent from March.
examples.uz: Shahar avtobus yo‘lkirasi martdan besh foizga oshadi.

examples.t: Bus fares in the city will rise by five per cent from March, the council announced on Tuesday.
examples.uz: Shahar avtobus yo‘lkirasi martdan besh foizga oshadi, deb e’lon qildi kengash seshanba kuni.

examples.t: According to the mayor, the money will fund new routes.
examples.uz: Mer aytishicha, bu mablag‘ yangi yo‘nalishlarga sarflanadi.

scenes.say_native: Yangilik „inverted pyramid“, ya’ni teskari piramida tartibida yoziladi: eng muhim ma’lumot boshida, tafsilotlar keyinroq. Birinchi jumla — „lead“ — kim, nima, qachon, qayerda va nima uchun degan savollarga javob beradi. Sarlavha qisqa bo‘ladi va ko‘pincha hozirgi zamonda yoziladi, hatto voqea o‘tgan bo‘lsa ham: „City bus fares to rise by five per cent“. Har bir fikr manbaga bog‘lanadi: „the council announced“, „according to the mayor“. Oddiy fe’l „said“ eng yaxshi, chunki neytral. O‘zbek maqolalari ko‘pincha tarix bilan boshlanadi, inglizcha yangilik esa asosiy faktdan boshlanadi.
scenes.say: News is written in an inverted pyramid: the most important facts come first and details follow. The first sentence, the lead, answers who, what, when and where. Headlines are short and often use the present tense: city bus fares to rise by five per cent. Every claim needs a source: the council announced, or according to the mayor.
scenes.say_uz: Yangilik teskari piramida tartibida yoziladi: eng muhim faktlar boshida, tafsilotlar keyin. Birinchi jumla kim, nima, qachon va qayerda savollariga javob beradi. Sarlavha qisqa va ko‘pincha hozirgi zamonda bo‘ladi. Har bir da’vo manbaga bog‘lanadi.

scenes.title: Xato: yangilikda shaxsiy fikr va uzun lead
board: ✗ Sadly, the council made a terrible choice.
✓ The council voted 7–4 to close the library.

examples.t: The council voted seven to four to close the library on Main Street.
examples.uz: Kengash yetti ovozga qarshi to‘rt ovoz bilan Main Street kutubxonasini yopishga ovoz berdi.

examples.t: The company said the delay was caused by a supplier.
examples.uz: Kompaniya kechikishga yetkazib beruvchi sabab bo‘lgan, dedi.

scenes.say_native: Yangilik yozishda uchta tipik xato bor. Birinchisi — baholovchi so‘zlar: „terrible choice“ muallifning fikri. Faktni ayting: „The council voted seven to four to close the library“. Ikkinchisi — juda uzun birinchi jumla: o‘n besh-yigirma besh so‘zdan iborat bo‘lsin. Uchinchisi — fe’l tanlash: „claimed“ — „da’vo qildi“ — shubha bildiradi, shuning uchun „said“ o‘rniga uni ishlatsangiz, o‘quvchi sizni tarafkash deb o‘ylaydi. Faqat sud yoki isbotlanmagan holatda „alleged“ ishlating. O‘zbekcha publitsistikada baho ko‘p uchraydi, inglizcha yangilikda esa baho faqat sharh bo‘limida bo‘ladi.
scenes.say: Three typical errors. Evaluative words like terrible choice are the writer's opinion. State the fact: the council voted seven to four to close the library. Do not write a forty-word lead. And choose verbs carefully. Claimed suggests doubt, so use said unless the matter is genuinely unproven: the company said the delay was caused by a supplier.
scenes.say_uz: Uchta tipik xato. Terrible choice kabi baholovchi so‘zlar muallif fikri: faktni ayting. Qirq so‘zli lead yozmang. Fe’lni ehtiyotkorlik bilan tanlang: claimed shubha bildiradi, shuning uchun isbotlanmagan holatdan tashqari said ishlating.

scenes.title: Mashq: lead yozing
board: Facts: Hotel Orient · fire on Sunday · 40 guests evacuated · no injuries · cause unknown
Write a one-sentence lead + a headline
scenes.say_native: Faktlar: Orient mehmonxonasida yakshanba kuni yong‘in chiqdi, qirq mehmon evakuatsiya qilindi, jabrlanganlar yo‘q, sabab noma’lum. Bitta jumlalik lead va qisqa sarlavha yozing. Eng muhim ma’lumot boshida bo‘lsin va baho bermang. Javobni baland ovozda ayting.
scenes.say: The facts are these. Fire at the Hotel Orient on Sunday. Forty guests evacuated. No injuries. Cause unknown. Write a one-sentence lead and a short headline. Put the most important information first and give no opinion.
scenes.say_uz: Faktlar: yakshanba kuni Orient mehmonxonasida yong‘in, qirq mehmon evakuatsiya qilindi, jabrlanganlar yo‘q, sabab noma’lum. Bitta jumlalik lead va qisqa sarlavha yozing. Muhim ma’lumot birinchi, baho yo‘q.

scenes.title: Javob: lead va sarlavha
board: Headline: Fire forces 40 hotel guests to flee
Lead: Forty guests were evacuated from the Hotel Orient on Sunday after a fire, but nobody was hurt.
The cause is not yet known.

examples.t: Forty guests were evacuated from the Hotel Orient on Sunday after a fire broke out, but nobody was hurt.
examples.uz: Yakshanba kuni Orient mehmonxonasida yong‘in chiqqach qirq mehmon evakuatsiya qilindi, lekin hech kim jarohat olmadi.

scenes.say_native: Namunaviy sarlavha: „Fire forces forty hotel guests to flee“. Lead: „Forty guests were evacuated from the Hotel Orient on Sunday after a fire broke out, but nobody was hurt.“ Keyin: „The cause of the fire is not yet known.“ Lead da kim — qirq mehmon, nima — evakuatsiya, qayerda — mehmonxona, qachon — yakshanba. „Break out“ — yong‘in yoki mojaro chiqmoq. „Is not yet known“ — hali noma’lum, bu taxmin qilmaslikning to‘g‘ri usuli. Sizning leadingizda to‘rt savolga javob bo‘lsa va fikr qo‘shilmagan bo‘lsa, a’lo.
scenes.say: A model headline: fire forces forty hotel guests to flee. The lead: forty guests were evacuated from the Hotel Orient on Sunday after a fire broke out, but nobody was hurt. Then: the cause of the fire is not yet known. The lead answers who, what, where and when, and it adds no opinion.
scenes.say_uz: Namunaviy sarlavha: yong‘in qirq mehmonni qochishga majbur qildi. Lead: yakshanba kuni Orient mehmonxonasida yong‘in chiqqach qirq mehmon evakuatsiya qilindi, lekin hech kim jarohat olmadi. Keyin: yong‘in sababi hali noma’lum. Lead kim, nima, qayerda va qachon savollariga javob beradi.

scenes.title: Fakt va fikr

examples.t: Unemployment fell to 4.2 per cent in May.
examples.uz: Ishsizlik may oyida 4,2 foizga tushdi.

examples.t: The new policy is arguably the best thing to happen to the economy.
examples.uz: Yangi siyosat iqtisodiyot uchun ehtimol eng yaxshi voqea.

examples.t: The minister slammed the so-called experts.
examples.uz: Vazir shunday deb ataladigan mutaxassislarni qattiq tanqid qildi.

scenes.say_native: Fakt tekshirilishi mumkin: „Unemployment fell to four point two per cent in May“. Fikr — baho yoki ishonch: „This is the best policy“. Fikrni belgilovchi so‘zlar bor: „arguably“ — dalil keltirish mumkin bo‘lgan holda, „it seems“, „I believe“. Ayniqsa „loaded words“ — hissiy yuklangan so‘zlarga e’tibor bering: „slammed“ — qattiq tanqid qildi, „so-called“ — go‘yo shunday deb ataladigan, ya’ni ishonchsizlik bildiradi. Bu so‘zlar neytral ko‘rinadi, lekin o‘quvchini yo‘naltiradi. Raqam ham fikr bo‘lishi mumkin: „only four per cent“ degandagi „only“ baho beradi. O‘qiyotganda: bu tekshirsa bo‘ladigan gapmi yoki baho?
scenes.say: A fact can be checked: unemployment fell to four point two per cent in May. An opinion is a judgement: this is the best policy. Opinion signals include arguably, it seems and I believe. Watch loaded words too. Slammed and so-called look neutral, but they steer the reader. Even a number can carry opinion: the word only in only four per cent is a judgement.
scenes.say_uz: Fakt tekshirilishi mumkin. Fikr — baho. Fikr belgilari: arguably, it seems, I believe. Yuklangan so‘zlarga ham e’tibor bering: slammed va so-called neytral ko‘rinadi, lekin o‘quvchini yo‘naltiradi. Hatto only so‘zi ham baho beradi.

scenes.title: Xato: fikrni fakt deb o‘qish
board: ✗ The strike is obviously damaging the economy.
✓ Analysts estimate the strike costs £30m a day.

examples.t: Analysts estimate that the strike costs thirty million pounds a day.
examples.uz: Tahlilchilarning hisobicha, ish tashlash kuniga o‘ttiz million funtga tushadi.

examples.t: A survey of twelve hundred adults found that sixty per cent support the plan.
examples.uz: O‘n ikki yuz kattalar o‘rtasidagi so‘rov ularning oltmish foizi rejani qo‘llab-quvvatlashini aniqladi.

scenes.say_native: O‘quvchi sifatida eng katta xato — baholovchi gapni fakt deb qabul qilish. „The strike is obviously damaging the economy“ da „obviously“ — aniq-ravshan, bu o‘quvchini rozi bo‘lishga undaydi. Fakt manbali bo‘ladi: „Analysts estimate that the strike costs thirty million pounds a day“. „Everyone knows“ — hamma biladi — dalil emas, bosim. Yaxshi manba raqamni ham, namunani ham ko‘rsatadi: „A survey of twelve hundred adults found that sixty per cent support the plan“. Yozuvchi sifatida esa aksincha: fikringizni „I believe“ yoki „in my view“ bilan belgilang, shunda o‘quvchi sizga ishonadi va aldanganini his qilmaydi.
scenes.say: As a reader, the biggest mistake is to take a judgement for a fact. The strike is obviously damaging the economy pushes you to agree. A fact has a source: analysts estimate that the strike costs thirty million pounds a day. Everyone knows is pressure, not evidence. A good source gives the sample too: a survey of twelve hundred adults found sixty per cent support the plan.
scenes.say_uz: O‘quvchi sifatida eng katta xato — bahoni fakt deb olish. Obviously o‘quvchini rozi bo‘lishga undaydi. Fakt manbali bo‘ladi. Everyone knows dalil emas, bosim. Yaxshi manba namunani ham ko‘rsatadi.

scenes.title: Mashq: fakt yoki fikr
board: 2) The company is a disaster for the town.
3) The mayor admitted the plan was flawed.
scenes.say_native: To‘rtta gapni tinglang va har birini „fact“ yoki „opinion“ deb belgilang. Uchinchi gapda fe’lga e’tibor bering: „admitted“ — tan oldi — u faktmi, bahomi? Javoblaringizni baland ovozda ayting.
scenes.say: Label each of four sentences as fact or opinion. One: the company employs two thousand four hundred people. Two: the company is a disaster for the town. Three: the mayor admitted the plan was flawed. Four: profits fell by eight per cent. Look carefully at the verb in sentence three.
scenes.say_uz: To‘rtta gapni fakt yoki fikr deb belgilang. Bir: kompaniya ikki ming to‘rt yuz kishini ishga oladi. Ikki: kompaniya shahar uchun falokat. Uch: mer reja nuqsonli ekanini tan oldi. To‘rt: foyda sakkiz foizga kamaydi. Uchinchi gapdagi fe’lga e’tibor bering.

scenes.title: Javoblar: fakt va fikr
board: 1) fact · 2) opinion · 3) mixed: ‘admitted’ is loaded · 4) fact

examples.t: The mayor said the plan was flawed.
examples.uz: Mer rejada nuqson bor, dedi.

scenes.say_native: Birinchi: fakt, chunki xodimlar sonini tekshirish mumkin. Ikkinchi: fikr, „disaster“ — baho. Uchinchi: aralash. „Admitted“ fe’li mer aybdor bo‘lgandek taassurot beradi, ya’ni yuklangan so‘z. Neytral variant: „The mayor said the plan was flawed“. To‘rtinchi: fakt, chunki foyda pasayishini hisobotdan tekshirish mumkin. Bu mashqning asosiy saboqi: neytral ko‘rinadigan fe’l ham hukm chiqarishi mumkin. „Admit“ va „confess“ aybni bildiradi, „say“ va „state“ esa neytral. Shuning uchun maqola o‘qiganda fe’llarga e’tibor bering.
scenes.say: One is a fact, because the number of employees can be checked. Two is an opinion, because disaster is a judgement. Three is mixed. The verb admitted suggests guilt, so it is loaded. A neutral version is: the mayor said the plan was flawed. Four is a fact, because the fall in profit can be verified in a report.
scenes.say_uz: Bir — fakt, xodimlar sonini tekshirish mumkin. Ikki — fikr, disaster baho. Uch — aralash: admitted fe’li aybdorlik taassurotini beradi, neytral variant said. To‘rt — fakt, foydaning pasayishini hisobotdan tekshirish mumkin.

scenes.title: Dialog: radio intervyu
board: Host: Mark · Guest: Dr Hale, hospital director
Listen: what is her key message?
How does she use a bridge?
scenes.say_native: Endi radio intervyuni tinglang. Boshlovchi Mark kasalxona direktori doktor Heyldan so‘raydi. Quyidagiga e’tibor bering: doktor Heylning asosiy xabari nima va u ko‘prikni qanday ishlatadi. Tinglab, javobni eslab qoling.
scenes.say: Mark: Dr Hale, patients are waiting eight hours in your emergency department. Isn't that a failure? Dr Hale: I understand the frustration, and I am sorry for every long wait. What matters most is that the sickest patients are always seen first. We have hired twelve new nurses, and waiting times will fall by the end of the year. Mark: But will they fall by enough? Dr Hale: Our target is four hours, and we will publish our progress every month.
scenes.say_uz: Mark: Doktor Heyl, shoshilinch bo‘limingizda bemorlar sakkiz soat kutmoqda. Bu muvaffaqiyatsizlik emasmi? Doktor Heyl: Norozilikni tushunaman va har bir uzoq kutish uchun afsusdaman. Eng muhimi, eng og‘ir bemorlar doim birinchi ko‘riladi. Biz o‘n ikki yangi hamshira yolladik va yil oxirigacha kutish vaqti qisqaradi. Mark: Lekin yetarlicha qisqaradimi? Doktor Heyl: Maqsadimiz to‘rt soat va har oy yutuqlarimizni e’lon qilamiz.

scenes.title: Mashq: intervyuni tahlil qiling
board: 2) Which bridge phrase does she use?
3) What numerical target and promise does she give?
scenes.say_native: Uchta savolga javob bering. Birinchi: doktor Heylning asosiy xabari nima? Ikkinchi: qaysi ko‘prik iborasidan foydalandi? Uchinchi: qanday raqamli maqsad va va’da berdi? Javobni baland ovozda ayting.
scenes.say: Answer three questions about the interview. What is Dr Hale's key message? Which bridge phrase does she use? What numerical target and what promise does she give?
scenes.say_uz: Intervyu bo‘yicha uchta savolga javob bering. Doktor Heylning asosiy xabari nima? U qaysi ko‘prik iborasini ishlatadi? Qanday raqamli maqsad va va’da beradi?

scenes.title: Javoblar: radio intervyu
board: 1) The sickest patients are always seen first

examples.t: What matters most is that the sickest patients are always seen first.
examples.uz: Eng muhimi, eng og‘ir bemorlar doim birinchi ko‘riladi.

scenes.say_native: Birinchi: asosiy xabar — eng og‘ir bemorlar doim birinchi ko‘riladi. Ikkinchi: ko‘prik iborasi — „What matters most is…“. Uchinchi: maqsad to‘rt soat va har oy yutuqni e’lon qilish. Diqqat qiling, doktor Heyl avval tan oldi: „I am sorry for every long wait“, keyin ko‘prik, keyin raqam va hisobot va’dasi berdi. Jurnalist ikkinchi savolda bosim o‘tkazdi, u esa yana aniq raqam bilan javob berdi, himoyaga o‘tmadi. „Frustration“ — norozilik, „waiting times will fall“ — kutish vaqti qisqaradi. Bunday tartib ishonchni oshiradi.
scenes.say: One: the sickest patients are always seen first. Two: what matters most is. Three: a four-hour target and monthly progress reports. Notice the order. Dr Hale apologises, bridges to her message, then gives numbers and a promise to report. When pressed, she answers with another figure and does not become defensive.
scenes.say_uz: Bir: eng og‘ir bemorlar doim birinchi ko‘riladi. Ikki: what matters most is. Uch: to‘rt soatlik maqsad va oylik hisobotlar. Tartibga e’tibor bering: avval uzr, keyin ko‘prik, keyin raqamlar va hisobot va’dasi. Bosim ostida ham himoyaga o‘tmaydi.

scenes.title: Dialog: tahririyatda
board: Listen: what does Priya want to change?
scenes.say_native: Ikkinchi dialog — tahririyatdagi suhbat. Muharrir Priya muxbir Semning maqolasini ko‘rib chiqadi. Tinglang: Priya nimani o‘zgartirmoqchi va nima uchun „claimed“ so‘zini rad etadi.
scenes.say: Priya: Sam, your draft is strong, but the lead is too long. Start with what happened. Sam: Okay. The mayor claimed the road would reopen in May. Priya: Use said. Claimed suggests she is lying, and we have no evidence of that. Also, you wrote the decision was shameful. That is your opinion, so take it out or attribute it to a named source. Sam: I will quote the residents' association instead.
scenes.say_uz: Priya: Sem, qoralamangiz yaxshi, lekin lead juda uzun. Nima bo‘lganidan boshlang. Sem: Yaxshi. Mer yo‘l maygacha ochiladi deb da’vo qildi. Priya: Said ishlating. Claimed u yolg‘on gapirayotganini ko‘rsatadi, bizda buning dalili yo‘q. Yana, qarorni sharmandali deb yozibsiz. Bu sizning fikringiz, olib tashlang yoki ismli manbaga bog‘lang. Sem: Uning o‘rniga aholi uyushmasidan iqtibos keltiraman.

scenes.title: Mashq: tahrir qaydlari
board: 1) Which two changes does Priya request?
3) How will Sam fix the opinion?
scenes.say_native: Uchta savolga javob bering. Birinchi: Priya qaysi ikkita o‘zgarishni so‘raydi? Ikkinchi: „claimed“ nega muammo? Uchinchi: Sem fikr muammosini qanday hal qiladi? Javobni baland ovozda ayting.
scenes.say: Answer three questions about the editor's notes. Which two changes does Priya request? Why is the word claimed a problem? How will Sam solve the problem of opinion in his draft?
scenes.say_uz: Muharrir qaydlari bo‘yicha uchta savolga javob bering. Priya qaysi ikkita o‘zgarishni so‘raydi? Claimed so‘zi nega muammo? Sem fikr muammosini qanday hal qiladi?

scenes.title: Javoblar: tahririyat
board: 1) Shorten the lead; remove the opinion

examples.t: Take it out or attribute it to a named source.
examples.uz: Uni olib tashlang yoki ismli manbaga bog‘lang.

scenes.say_native: Birinchi: Priya leadni qisqartirishni va „shameful“ degan fikrni olib tashlashni so‘raydi. Ikkinchi: „claimed“ shubha bildiradi, ya’ni mer yolg‘on gapirayotgandek. Uchinchi: Sem aholi uyushmasidan iqtibos keltiradi, shunda fikr muallifniki emas, manbaniki bo‘ladi. „Attribute to“ — kimgadir bog‘lamoq, „named source“ — ismi aytilgan manba. Bu jurnalistika qoidasi: fikr kerak bo‘lsa, uni egasi bilan bering. Maqola ishonchli bo‘lishi uchun har bir baholovchi gapga kim aytgani ko‘rsatiladi.
scenes.say: One: Priya wants a shorter lead and no opinion in the text. Two: claimed suggests the mayor is lying. Three: Sam will quote the residents' association, so the judgement belongs to a named source and not to the writer. To attribute something to someone means to say who said it. If you need an opinion in a news story, give it an owner.
scenes.say_uz: Bir: Priya qisqaroq lead va matnda fikr bo‘lmasligini xohlaydi. Ikki: claimed merning yolg‘on gapirayotganini bildiradi. Uch: Sem aholi uyushmasidan iqtibos keltiradi, shunda baho muallifniki emas, ismli manbaniki bo‘ladi. Yangilikda fikr kerak bo‘lsa, unga egasini ko‘rsating.

scenes.title: Talaffuz: tempo va pauza
board: Slow down for numbers: forty / fourteen
Fall at the end of statements

examples.t: The deficit is fourteen million, not forty.
examples.uz: Kamomad o‘n to‘rt million, qirq emas.

examples.t: What matters most is… safety.
examples.uz: Eng muhimi… xavfsizlik.

scenes.say_native: Media intervyusida talaffuz ham xabarning bir qismi. Raqamlarda ehtiyot bo‘ling: „fourteen“ ning urg‘usi „teen“ da, „forty“ ning urg‘usi „for“ da. „Fourteen million, not forty“ — bu farqni aniq ayting. Ikkinchi: asosiy so‘zdan oldin qisqa pauza qiling: „What matters most is… safety“. Pauza so‘zni kuchaytiradi va sizga o‘ylash vaqti beradi. Uchinchi: darak gapni pasayuvchi ohang bilan tugating, shunda ishonchli eshitiladi. To‘rtinchi: „um“, „you know“ kabi to‘ldiruvchilar ko‘paysa, ishonch pasayadi; ularni jimlik bilan almashtiring. O‘zbek tilida pauza ko‘pincha noaniqlik belgisi, inglizchada esa ishonch belgisi.
scenes.say: Delivery is part of the message. Take care with numbers: fourteen is stressed on the last syllable, forty on the first. Say clearly: fourteen million, not forty. Pause before the key word: what matters most is, safety. A pause adds weight and gives you thinking time. Finish statements with a falling tone, and replace fillers like um and you know with silence.
scenes.say_uz: Yetkazish uslubi xabarning bir qismi. Raqamlarga ehtiyot bo‘ling: fourteen oxirgi bo‘g‘inda, forty birinchi bo‘g‘inda urg‘u oladi. Asosiy so‘zdan oldin pauza qiling. Darak gapni pasayuvchi ohang bilan tugating, to‘ldiruvchilarni jimlik bilan almashtiring.

scenes.title: Yakuniy topshiriq: mini intervyu
board: You are the CEO of a food-delivery start-up
Q1: Why were your prices raised?
scenes.say_native: Siz oziq-ovqat yetkazib berish startapining rahbarisiz. Ikkita savolga qirq soniya ichida javob bering. Birinchi savol: narxlarni nega oshirdingiz? Ikkinchi: kuryerlarga adolatli to‘lanyaptimi? Har javobda tan olish, ko‘prik va qisqa soundbite bo‘lsin. Javoblarni baland ovozda ayting.
scenes.say: You are the chief executive of a food delivery start-up. Answer two questions in forty seconds. One: why did you raise your prices? Two: are your riders paid fairly? In each answer, acknowledge, bridge and finish with a short soundbite.
scenes.say_uz: Siz oziq-ovqat yetkazish startapining bosh direktorisiz. Qirq soniyada ikkita savolga javob bering. Bir: nega narxlarni oshirdingiz? Ikki: kuryerlarga adolatli to‘lanyaptimi? Har javobda tan oling, ko‘prik qiling va qisqa soundbite bilan tugating.

scenes.title: Javob: mini intervyu namunasi
board: Prices: fuel + rider pay up → 40 pence rise
Riders: minimum pay guaranteed, weekly bonus
Soundbite: Good service needs fair pay.

examples.t: Good service starts with fair pay.
examples.uz: Yaxshi xizmat adolatli to‘lovdan boshlanadi.

scenes.say_native: Namunaviy javob. Birinchi savol: „It is a fair question. Our costs have risen, and we added forty pence per order to protect rider pay. What matters most is that customers see the fee clearly.“ Ikkinchi: „I understand the concern. Every rider has a guaranteed minimum hourly pay and a weekly bonus. Good service starts with fair pay.“ Soundbite — „Good service starts with fair pay“, olti so‘z. „Per order“ — har buyurtma uchun. „Guaranteed“ — kafolatlangan. Sizning javobingizda tan olish, ko‘prik va qisqa shior bo‘lsa, topshiriq bajarilgan.
scenes.say: A model answer. One: it is a fair question. Our costs have risen, and we added forty pence per order to protect rider pay. What matters most is that customers see the fee clearly. Two: I understand the concern. Every rider has a guaranteed minimum hourly pay and a weekly bonus. Good service starts with fair pay.
scenes.say_uz: Namunaviy javob. Bir: bu o‘rinli savol. Xarajatlarimiz oshdi va kuryerlar to‘lovini himoya qilish uchun har buyurtmaga qirq pens qo‘shdik. Eng muhimi, mijozlar to‘lovni aniq ko‘radi. Ikki: tashvishni tushunaman. Har bir kuryerga soatiga kafolatlangan minimal to‘lov va haftalik bonus bor. Yaxshi xizmat adolatli to‘lovdan boshlanadi.

scenes.title: Takrorlash
board: Prepare 3 points · buy time · don’t speculate
Bridge back to the key message
scenes.say_native: Bugungi darsni jamlaymiz. Intervyuga uchta asosiy fikr, qiyin savollar va aniq raqamlar bilan tayyorlaning; taxmin qilmang va „no comment“ dan qoching. Asosiy xabarga ko‘prik iboralari bilan qayting va o‘n besh so‘zlik soundbite ayting. Yangilikda eng muhim fakt birinchi turadi, manba ko‘rsatiladi va „said“ neytral fe’l hisoblanadi. Fakt tekshiriladi, fikr esa baho; yuklangan so‘zlar va „only“ kabi so‘zlar ham yo‘naltiradi. Talaffuzda raqamlarni aniq ayting va pauzadan foydalaning.
scenes.say: Let's review. Prepare three points and your figures. Do not speculate and avoid a cold no comment. Bridge back to your key message and offer a short soundbite. In news writing, the key fact comes first, claims have sources, and said is the neutral verb. A fact can be checked, an opinion is a judgement, and loaded words steer the reader.
scenes.say_uz: Takrorlaymiz. Uchta fikr va raqamlarni tayyorlang. Taxmin qilmang va sovuq no comment dan saqlaning. Asosiy xabarga ko‘prik bilan qayting. Yangilikda asosiy fakt birinchi, da’volar manbali va said neytral fe’l. Fakt tekshiriladi, fikr baho, yuklangan so‘zlar o‘quvchini yo‘naltiradi.

scenes.title: Uyga vazifa
board: Homework: record a mock media interview
Use: acknowledge · bridge · soundbite · one fact with a source
scenes.say_native: Uyga vazifa: soxta media intervyusini yozib oling. Do‘stingiz yoki o‘zingiz uchta savol tayyorlang, ulardan biri qiyin bo‘lsin. Ikki-uch daqiqa gapiring. Muvaffaqiyat mezoni: har javobda tan olish, ko‘prik iborasi, manbasi bor bitta fakt va kamida bitta qisqa soundbite. Tinglab, „no comment“ va to‘ldiruvchilarni sanang. Keyingi darsda badiiy matnlarni tahlil qilishni o‘rganamiz.
scenes.say: Your homework is to record a mock media interview. Prepare three questions, one of them hard, and speak for two to three minutes. In every answer, acknowledge, bridge, give one fact with a source and add a short soundbite. Next time we turn to analysing literary texts.
scenes.say_uz: Uyga vazifa: soxta media intervyusini yozib oling. Uchta savol tayyorlang, bittasi qiyin bo‘lsin, ikki-uch daqiqa gapiring. Har javobda tan oling, ko‘prik qiling, manbali bitta fakt va qisqa soundbite qo‘shing. Keyingi safar badiiy matnlarni tahlil qilamiz.

homework_uz: Soxta media intervyusini yozib oling: uchta savol (bittasi qiyin), ikki-uch daqiqa. Har javobda tan olish, ko‘prik iborasi, manbali bitta fakt va qisqa soundbite bo‘lsin. Keyingi darsda badiiy matn tahlilini o‘rganamiz.

quiz.q: Which reply is best to a hostile question?
options: I understand the concern. What matters most is that customers are safe.
Off the record, it’s a mess.
quiz.why_uz: Tan olish va ko‘prik asosiy xabarga qaytaradi.

options: A background noise in a recording

quiz.q: Why should you avoid ‘off the record’?
options: You must assume everything can be printed
quiz.why_uz: Hamma gap yozib olinishi mumkin deb o‘ylash xavfsiz.

quiz.q: What comes first in an inverted pyramid?
quiz.why_uz: Teskari piramidada eng muhim fakt boshida.

quiz.q: Which is the most neutral reporting verb?
quiz.why_uz: “Said” neytral, boshqalari shubha yoki aybni bildiradi.

options: Profits fell by eight per cent.

quiz.q: Which headline is in news style?
options: Fire forced forty guests to be fleeing
Fire forces 40 hotel guests to flee
The terrible fire that scared guests
Guests and the fire in the hotel

quiz.why_uz: Fourteen — oxirgi, forty — birinchi bo‘g‘inda urg‘u.

quiz.q: In a news story, how should you include a judgement?
options: Attribute it to a named source
